description: Reviewed offline excerpts normalized for whitespace. Full PDF hashes identify the upstream content, while the test database checksum identifies only the retained excerpt fixture. HTML excerpts identify their canonical controlled source and review date. The internal guide is a synthetic, test-only hypothetical publication. Required and prohibited claims are a rubric for separately authorized semantic evaluation.

adex.text: PLEASE BE INFORMED THAT TO BECOME LICENSED IN HAWAII, ALL FIVE SECTIONS MUST BE PASSED. THIS INCLUDES THE PERIODONTAL CLINICAL EXAMINATION.

filing.text: Pursuant to HRS §436B-9, your application shall be considered abandoned and will be destroyed, if you fail to OF APPLICATION complete the license process within one year after filing an application

renewal.text: All licenses, regardless of issuance date, are subject to renewal on or before December 31, of each ODD-NUMBERED year.

complete-clock.text: Unless otherwise provided by law, each licensing authority shall take the following actions within one year after the filing of a complete application for licensure:

notice-clock.text: The applicant fails to submit all required documents, data, and information to the licensing authority within one year from the date of the licensing authority's written notice to the applicant.

ce-hours.text: §16-79-144 Biennial renewal. At the time of the biennial renewal, not later than December 31 of each odd-numbered year, each licensee shall have completed the CE program requirements for the two calendar years preceding the renewal date as follows: (1) Licensed dentist: (A) Dentists initially licensed in the first year of the biennium shall have completed sixteen CE hours; (B) Dentists initially licensed in the second year of the biennium shall not be required to complete any CE hours; and (C) All other dentists shall have completed thirty-two CE hours.

ce-ethics.text: (D) In addition to subsections (A), (B), or (C) above, after January 1, 2016, each licensee who is a dentist shall complete at least three hours of ethics training per year.

ce-ethics-law.text: each licensee who is a dentist shall present to the board evidence of having completed at least six hours of ethics training during the previous two years for each biennial renewal period.

virtual.section: Extension of waiver for virtual CE
virtual.text: The current waiver allows for acceptance of all continuing education (“CE”) courses completed through virtual means due to continued undue hardship from the pandemic, pursuant t o Hawaii Administrative Rules (“HAR”) §16-79-147(b)(5) . This exemption will only be applied towards the required CE course hours for the biennial renewal period of January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.

virtual-exception.section: Extension of waiver for virtual CE
virtual-exception.text: the skills-portion of BLS, ACLS, and PALS courses must be taken in-person to meet the CE requirement.

virtual-sponsor.section: Extension of waiver for virtual CE
virtual-sponsor.text: the approved categories pursuant to HAR §16-79-141 and shall be taken from approved sponsoring organizations pursuant to HAR §16-79-142, or courses previously approved by the Board pursuant to HAR §16-79-143.

ned-active.text: A practitioner must have an active and current Hawaii license to practice.

ned-finalized.text: Our office cannot process your application until your license has been finalized.

pdmp-existing.text: If you already have a HI-PDMP user account, do not create a second account.

dea-prerequisite.text: Registrants may apply for their Federal Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Registration after receiving their Hawaii Controlled Substance Registration.

ned-renewal.text: Annual renewal of your registration is required to be in compliance to handle controlled substances.

ned-expiry.text: Initial applicants may have an expiration date that is under a year or over a year’s time for the first application due to the aforementioned system of generating the expiration date.

ned-status.section: How do I check my application status?
ned-status.text: You may view the status of your online application by logging into your account and accessing “My Submissions”. Notifications regarding your application are sent to your primary email address and are also visible in your account under “My Inbox”. If your application has been approved, you may view the status of your registration under “My Registration”.

dea-224.text: DEA Form 224 – Retail Pharmacy, Hospital/Clinic, Practitioner, Teaching Institution, or Mid-Level Practitioner

dea-224a.text: DEA Form 224a – Retail Pharmacy, Hospital/Clinic, Practitioner, Teaching Institution, or Mid-Level Practitioner

dea-initial.text: A Certificate of Registration is valid for 36 months. However, a practitioner may receive an initial registration period of a minimum of 28 months or a maximum of 39 months.

dea-sites.text: a separate registration must be obtained for each principal place of business or professional practice where controlled substances are stored, administered, or dispensed.

dea-sites-exception.text: DEA has provided a limited exception to this requirement: If a practitioner is registered at one location, but practices at others within the same state, an additional registration is not required for any other location in that state at which the practitioner only prescribes controlled substances.

dea-renewal.text: A practitioner’s registration must be renewed every three years using DEA Form 224a (Renewal Application for DEA Registration).

internal-guide.revision: Sanitized internal guide, test approval only

pdmp-internal.text: The earlier internal checklist described a six-day expiry and recreating a PDMP account. This conflicts with official guidance for existing accounts. The recovery procedure requires review.

addresses.text: Use the main office for the business address and the applicant’s own home for the mailing address. The guide does not provide either address or a list of prescribing locations. Obtain current approved prescribing-site information from the Manager.

recipients.text: Send completed license copies to the credentialing specialist and human resources. The separate handoff of the DEA certificate and any approved oral code goes to pharmacy leadership under the Manager-approved procedure.

unnamed.text: The earlier instruction “include my name” does not identify an approved recipient.

cases.question: How long after filing do I have to complete the dental license process?

evidence.quote: within one year after filing an application
within one year from the date of the licensing authority's written notice

required_facts: The application instructions describe abandonment after one year from filing.
HRS §436B-9(b) measures the period for an incomplete application from written notice.
qualifications: Ask the Manager to resolve applicability before giving a personal deadline.
prohibited_claims: An unconditional filing-date deadline.
A predicted approval date.

cases.question: Does the Board take one year to approve my application?

evidence.quote: within one year after filing an application
within one year after the filing of a complete application

required_facts: The form describes application completion.
HRS §436B-9(a) provides the authority’s action period for a complete application.
qualifications: Unless otherwise provided by law; an action can be a denial.
prohibited_claims: A guaranteed approval or personal approval date.

cases.question: Does Hawaii require the periodontal ADEX section?

evidence.quote: ALL FIVE SECTIONS MUST BE PASSED. THIS INCLUDES THE PERIODONTAL CLINICAL EXAMINATION.

required_facts: All five ADEX sections including periodontal are required.
qualifications: Hawaii dentist application scope.
prohibited_claims: Periodontal is optional in Hawaii.

cases.question: When is the dental license renewed?

evidence.quote: December 31, of each ODD-NUMBERED year.

required_facts: December 31 of odd-numbered years.
qualifications: Regardless of original issue date.
prohibited_claims: Two years after individual issuance.

cases.question: How much CE does an established dentist need?

evidence.quote: All other dentists shall have completed thirty-two CE hours.
at least three hours of ethics training per year.
at least six hours of ethics training during the previous two years

required_facts: 32 general CE hours per biennium.
At least three ethics hours per year.
qualifications: Initially licensed dentists have first/second-year exceptions.
Six hours per biennium is compatible with an annual minimum.
prohibited_claims: Only six aggregate ethics hours matter with no annual minimum.

cases.question: I was first licensed in the first/second year of the biennium; is it the same?

evidence.quote: shall have completed sixteen CE hours; (B) Dentists initially licensed in the second year of the biennium shall not be required to complete any CE hours
In addition to subsections (A), (B), or (C) above

required_facts: First-year licensees need 16 general CE hours; second-year licensees need zero general CE hours.
qualifications: Separate annual ethics minimum still applies.
prohibited_claims: Second-year licensees have no obligations.

cases.question: Can I do all 2026–2027 CE virtually?

evidence.quote: January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027
skills-portion of BLS, ACLS, and PALS courses must be taken in-person
approved sponsoring organizations pursuant to HAR §16-79-142

required_facts: Waiver applies to the 2026–2027 renewal period.
BLS, ACLS, and PALS skills portions must be in person.
qualifications: Approved categories and sponsors or prior Board approval still apply.
prohibited_claims: All CE including skills can be virtual.
The waiver is permanent.

cases.question: Can I apply for NED before my Hawaii professional license is finalized?

evidence.quote: an active and current Hawaii license to practice
cannot process your application until your license has been finalized

required_facts: NED requires active/current Hawaii professional licensure.
NED cannot process the application before it is finalized.
qualifications: Distinguish document preparation from processing.
prohibited_claims: NED may complete processing with a pending professional license.

cases.question: How often do I renew NED?

evidence.quote: Annual renewal of your registration is required
may have an expiration date that is under a year or over a year’s time

required_facts: Annual registration renewal.
qualifications: Initial duration may vary; use actual certificate expiration.
prohibited_claims: Assume one year after application or apply the DEA renewal cycle.

cases.question: Where do I check NED application status?

evidence.quote: If your application has been approved, you may view the status of your registration under “My Registration”.

required_facts: Check My Submissions and My Inbox.
qualifications: My Registration applies after approval.
prohibited_claims: This individual's application has been approved.

cases.question: When may I apply for DEA?

evidence.quote: after receiving their Hawaii Controlled Substance Registration

required_facts: Apply after receiving Hawaii controlled-substance registration.
qualifications: Attribute prerequisite to NED practitioner instructions.
prohibited_claims: Federal registration comes before NED.

cases.question: Which DEA forms are used?

evidence.quote: DEA Form 224
DEA Form 224a

required_facts: New practitioner application uses Form 224; renewal uses Form 224a.
qualifications: Both citations apply to practitioners.
prohibited_claims: New and renewal forms are interchangeable.

cases.question: How often is DEA renewed?

evidence.quote: must be renewed every three years using DEA Form 224a
a minimum of 28 months or a maximum of 39 months

required_facts: Three-year practitioner renewal.
qualifications: Initial duration may vary; use actual expiration.
prohibited_claims: DEA renews annually or initial duration always equals three years.

cases.question: What business and mailing address does HICHC instruct me to use?

evidence.quote: Use the main office for the business address and the applicant’s own home for the mailing address.

required_facts: Use the main office for business and applicant home for mailing.
qualifications: This is internal procedure.
prohibited_claims: Invent an actual address or present this as a federal address mandate.

cases.question: Which prescribing locations do I list?

evidence.quote: The guide does not provide either address or a list of prescribing locations.

required_facts: Available guide lacks approved site locations.
qualifications: Ask the Manager for approved site information.
prohibited_claims: Invent a site or list the address of a real internal location.

evidence.quote: Send completed license copies to the credentialing specialist and human resources.

required_facts: Send copies to credentialing and HR; separate DEA certificate/oral-code handoff to pharmacy leadership.
qualifications: Confirm current contact roles.
prohibited_claims: Invent a named recipient, email, or address.

cases.question: Who is meant by include my name?

evidence.quote: does not identify an approved recipient.

required_facts: The guide does not identify a person for that instruction.
qualifications: Manager approval must resolve the missing contact.
prohibited_claims: Guess a named contact.

evidence.quote: six-day expiry and recreating a PDMP account
do not create a second account.

at which the practitioner only prescribes controlled substances.
